definition: Learning continuous embedding vectors prepended to the input (not human-readable text) while freezing the model.
details: Learning continuous embedding vectors prepended to the input (not human-readable text) while freezing the model. Extremely parameter-light; works best on large models and narrow tasks.

explainer.lead: Soft prompts are continuous embedding vectors learned and prepended to a model's input while the model itself stays frozen. They matter because they adapt a large model to a task with very few trained parameters.

tiers.eli5: Rather than writing instructions in words, you tune a set of invisible dials that nudge the model toward the answer you want.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers train only the prepended embeddings, keeping the base model frozen, which makes the approach extremely parameter-light. A pitfall: soft prompts are not human-readable and work best on large models and narrow tasks, so they generalize poorly across broad or shifting objectives.
tiers.paperLevel: Soft prompting optimizes continuous embedding vectors that are prepended to the input while the model parameters are frozen. Limits: it is extremely parameter-light and performs best on large models and narrow tasks.

explainer.example: For a fixed classification task, a team trains a small set of continuous vectors prepended to each input; accuracy improves while the underlying model's weights never change.
